summary: Masaaki Hattori is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta under Naoshiro Tsuji, Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and others. He held main posts at Kyoto University and Hanazono University.

Masaaki Nitta is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Fukui Prefectural College (attested 1983–1991) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).

Masaaki Noni is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Gadjin M. Nagao. He served at Ryukoku University as an assistant professor (attested 2003) and professor (attested 2013–2014).

Masaaki Sugiyama was a historian of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1970 to 1978 and held a post at Kyoto Women's University from circa 1981 to 1992.
Masaaki Tsuchiya works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kokugakuin University from circa 1979 to 1990 and held a post at Senshu University around 1996.

Masaharu Anesaki was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, Kiel University, and with scholars including Paul Deussen. He was a professor at the University of Tokyo and directed its library.

Masaharu Imai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology who earned a doctorate at Tokyo University of Education. He held posts at Ibaraki University and the University of Tsukuba, where he became professor emeritus in 2006.

Masahide Mori specializes in Buddhist studies and history. He studied at Nagoya University, the University of London, and SOAS under Tadeusz Skorupski, and he held faculty posts at Nagoya University, Koyasan University, and Kanazawa University.
Masahiro Asada is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University from around 1963 to 1971. He later served there as an assistant professor from circa 1985 to 1995.

Masahiro Inami specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral coursework at Hiroshima University (circa 1983–1990) and held posts at Tokyo Gakugei University from circa 1996 onward.

Masahiro Kusunoki was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University from circa 1947 to 1953. He later served as a professor of religious studies and the history of religion at Tohoku University (~1974–1985).

Masahiro Shimoda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his degrees at the University of Tokyo and studying at the University of Delhi. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023) and Musashino University (2023).
Masahiro Takano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University. He also held a post as a librarian at Taisho University (attested 1995).

Masakazu Tanaka is a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University and the London School of Economics. He served as an assistant professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019) and became vice president and professor at the Professional Institute of International Fashion in 2019.

Masako Keta is a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi. She served as an assistant professor and professor at Kanazawa University before holding a professorship in philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000–2018).
Masamichi Asukai was a scholar of Japanology and history. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1954 to 1964 and later held an academic post there from approximately 1975 to 1998.

Masamichi Ichigo is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He held professorships at Kyoto Sangyo University, Otani University, and Kyoto Koka Women's University.
Masamichi Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied under Helmut Krasser in 2006 and earned a Dr.phil. from the University of Vienna (attested 2010).
Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and an assistant professor in the Faculty of Literature (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

Masanori Shono is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has held positions as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).
